evidence: The official akandykeller/Wave_RNNs repository currently has three GitHub forks and a single official commit (2630b88ce772a1945b69b6b369ce428202586400).

lute47lillo/Wave_RNNs and HOIAN17/Wave_RNNs have parent=akandykeller/Wave_RNNs, size 18, and pushed_at equal to the official source's 2024-03-15 push; classify as passive forks, not execution evidence.

zhangyuyi99/Wave_RNNs is a true divergent fork, four commits ahead of the official initial commit. The diff adds a CA/ cellular-automata task/notebook/sweeps and makes small edits to adding/copy/environment files. No committed original-benchmark result artifacts were found in repository search, so classify as a non-comparable adaptation rather than replication.

Yoshimasa Kubo's July 2026 DW-RNN preprint independently reruns the standard wRNN baseline over five random seeds using the original training protocol on sMNIST, psMNIST, and nsCIFAR-10: 97.27±0.15%, 96.74±0.17%, and 54.30±0.79%. These values are close to Keller et al.'s published wRNN values (main-table 97.6%, 96.7%, 55.0%; recovered three-seed values include psMNIST 96.60±0.10 and nsCIFAR-10 54.70±0.42), providing partial non-author corroboration of benchmark performance.
This does not reproduce the full original suite or establish exact protocol identity for every reported number, and the DW-RNN preprint has not yet released its code.

new_or_updated_candidates.mechanism: Dendritic Wave RNN (DW-RNN) preserves the Wave-RNN's local circular recurrent convolution but replaces the linear input-to-hidden term with multiple sparse nonlinear basal-dendritic branches whose outputs are averaged before the recurrent update.
evidence: bioRxiv 2026.07.03.736415, posted July 9, 2026; not peer reviewed.
Five-seed test accuracy: sMNIST wRNN 97.27±0.15% vs DW-RNN 97.82±0.12% (+0.55 pp); psMNIST 96.74±0.17% vs 96.92±0.10% (+0.18 pp); noisy sequential CIFAR-10 54.30±0.79% vs 55.65±0.55% (+1.35 pp).

The same hidden size (256), channels (16), batch size (128), recurrent filter size (3), hidden ReLU, and learning rate (1e-4) are reported for wRNN and DW-RNN on the three image tasks unless otherwise specified.
The dendritic pathway uses two basal branches per hidden unit with branch sparsity 0.5 across datasets; sMNIST/psMNIST use gain-controlled tanh (g_d=4), while nsCIFAR-10 uses LeakyReLU for stability.

Copy-task delays 0, 30, and 80 are reported as comparable between wRNN and DW-RNN, indicating the dendritic input modification does not visibly destroy the original wave-memory behavior, but the paper does not provide a compact numerical copy-task table.
Representative hidden-state plots retain diagonal traveling-wave patterns after the dendritic input intervention.
mechanistic_scope: The intervention is more specific than a generic larger RNN: the recurrent wave convolution is held fixed in form and the input integration pathway is changed to sparse nonlinear dendritic branches.

The paper does not report an explicit parameter-count-matched control or isolate branch count, sparsity, and nonlinearity in a factorial ablation, so the small accuracy gains cannot yet be attributed uniquely to a biological dendritic mechanism rather than added input-path expressivity/regularization.
The absolute gains are modest (+0.18 to +1.35 pp) and strongest on noisy sequential CIFAR-10; there is no language/audio/control evidence yet.
Training uses Adam, cross-entropy, gradient clipping, and standard gradient-based optimization; the learning rule itself is not biologically local.
This is a single-author preprint and code is explicitly described as still being organized for future public release; exact independent reproduction of DW-RNN is therefore not established.

rejected_or_qualified.lead: DW-RNN accuracy gains as proof that dendrites causally improve sequence learning
rejected_or_qualified.reason: The input-path intervention improves five-seed means, but no parameter-matched or component-factorial control separates dendritic nonlinear integration from added expressivity/regularization.
